claims.sentence: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering is organized as a 4-year program
The instruction is performed mostly in English
The total degree requires the acquisition of 240 ECTS credits, distributed at a pace of 60 credits per year
One credit corresponds to approximately 36 academic hours of student effort
Students take a total of 45 courses over the four years
For the Software Engineering, Data Science, and Security-Blockchain streams, the yearly course distribution is identical

These students take 12 core courses and 0 electives in the first year, 12 core and 0 electives in the second year, 10 core and 1 elective in the third year, and 6 core and 4 electives in the fourth year
The total for these streams is 40 core courses and 5 elective courses
For the Robotics stream, the distribution differs slightly
Students take 12 core and 0 electives in the first year, 12 core and 0 electives in the second year, 11 core and 0 electives in the third year, and 8 core and 2 electives in the fourth year
The total for this stream is 43 core courses and 2 elective courses
The first two years contain fundamental courses in mathematics, physics, and computer science and engineering

The body of knowledge includes Math, Physics, Algorithms and Complexity, Programming Languages, Software Development Fundamentals, Architecture and organization, Operating Systems, Computational Science, information management, and Networking and Communications

The primary objective is to provide a solid scientific and technical foundation, fostering skills in efficient program development, problem-solving using computer programs, and understanding computer system theory
In the third and fourth years, students select one of four streams
Software Engineering:** Combines system theory, computer science, and software engineering for careers in software engineering
Data Science:** Integrates intelligent systems, computer science, and data science to evaluate and interpret big data
Robotics:** Provides fundamental knowledge in mechanics, mechatronics, electrical engineering, control theory, and robotics
Security-Blockchain:** Focuses on information security, secure software design, and distributed ledger technologies such as cryptocurrencies and blockchain

The body of knowledge in the final two years includes Graphics and Visualization, Information Assurance and Security, Intelligent Systems, Parallel and Distributed Computing, Software Engineering, Systems Fundamentals, Human-Computer Interaction, Finance, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mathematical Physics, Robotics, and Control Engineering
Every year, students have a mandatory internship during the summer break
Internships typically start once the spring semester exam session is completed
Industrial:** Work in Innopolis University partner IT companies, primarily in Innopolis
Scientific:** Work in university labs on ongoing research and development tasks
Administrative:** Work in university departments on IT analysis, design, and implementation projects
Internships can also combine these three types
The credit distribution for internships is 14 credits in the first year, 10 in the second, 10 in the third, and 24 in the fourth, totaling 58 credits
An internship of 8 credits requires 288 hours of effort, approximately 7 weeks
At the end of the second year, students must pass a multidisciplinary exam to evaluate their comprehensive understanding of the discipline and ability to engage in system-oriented thinking
This exam ensures students can solve broadly-based IT problems before progressing to years three and four
Graduates are expected to know English at least at the level of IELTS 7
Admission requires a minimum IELTS level of 5
End of first year: IELTS 5.5
End of second year: IELTS 6
End of third year: IELTS 6.5
End of fourth year: IELTS 7
It is the student's responsibility to achieve these levels using university resources
Courses are organized using various teaching mechanisms: Class Lecture (Lc), Class Tutorial (Tut), Group Laboratory (Lab), and Individual Labs (IL)
Math and science courses typically follow the structure 2Lc-2Lab-2IL
Computer science and engineering courses follow the structure 2Lc-2Tut-2Lab
Technical courses follow the structure 2Lc-2Lab-2IL
Humanities courses follow the structure 2Lc-4IL
The evidence does not specify the exact titles of the 45 courses taken by students
The evidence does not detail the specific content of the multidisciplinary exam beyond its purpose
The evidence does not specify the credit value of individual courses, only the total credits per year and for internships
The evidence does not specify the duration or credit value of the final thesis, only the total internship credits
The evidence does not specify the exact resources provided by the university for language learning
